key_insight: Kraken makes speech-to-speech translation easier for LLMs by replacing hard-to-predict high-bitrate speech tokens with compact low-bitrate VQ tokens. It also conditions the model on source speech in two ways, helping preserve both meaning and speech characteristics like speaker identity and prosody.
problem_solved: This paper addresses two major S2ST challenges: predicting very large, high-bitrate speech token sequences with LLMs, and depending on scarce training data where source and target speech are ideally aligned in speaker identity and prosody.
method: Use low-bitrate speech tokens from single-layer vector quantization instead of high-bitrate discrete speech units.
Train the tokens to reconstruct SSL (self-supervised learning) features, making them more compact and model-friendly.
Apply dual-path source conditioning so the system can better use source speech content and paralinguistic cues during translation.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests a more practical route to building speech translation systems that are easier for LLMs to model and less dependent on perfectly aligned S2ST data. It may improve scalability, data efficiency, and the preservation of natural speech properties in translated output.

paper_title: Kraken: LLM-based Speech-to-Speech Translation via Low-bitrate VQ and Dual-path Source Conditioning
paper_authors: Hayato Futami, Hassan Shahmohammadi, Tushar Dhyani, Alkis Koudounas, Raphaël Lafargue
